question: Analyze sales performance. Calculate total revenue, identify the top five products by revenue, compare monthly revenue, detect missing values, and recommend three data-backed actions.

plan.goal: Analyze sales performance by calculating total revenue, ranking products by revenue, comparing revenue by month, quantifying missing and duplicate data, and producing outputs that support three data-backed actions.

steps.description: Create revenue as quantity multiplied by unit price and calculate total revenue.
Aggregate revenue by non-missing product, identify the top five products, and calculate their combined revenue share.
Parse order dates, aggregate revenue by calendar month, and calculate each month's revenue share.
Count missing values by column, total missing cells, and duplicate rows.
Provide product and monthly tables and charts to support three data-backed actions based on concentration, seasonality, and data-quality findings.

assumptions: Revenue is calculated as quantity multiplied by unit_price; pandas skips rows where either input is missing when summing, so those rows add nothing to revenue.

Missing product and date values are retained in the source data and counted in data-quality outputs, but rows with missing product are excluded from the product grouping because they cannot be assigned to a named product.
All valid order_date values are grouped by calendar month using YYYY-MM labels.
Duplicate rows are retained in revenue calculations because the question does not request deduplication.

code:
data = df.assign(
    revenue=df["quantity"] * df["unit_price"],
    parsed_order_date=pd.to_datetime(df["order_date"], errors="coerce")
)

emit_metric(
    "Total revenue",
    data["revenue"].sum(),
    check={"op": "sum", "columns": ["quantity", "unit_price"]}
)

# Full product groups are calculated before selecting the top five, so the
# independent check applies to complete groups rather than a truncated table.
product_revenue_all = (
    data.loc[data["product"].notna()]
    .groupby("product", as_index=False)["revenue"]
    .sum()
    .sort_values("revenue", ascending=False)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
emit_table(
    "Revenue by product",
    product_revenue_all,
    check={
        "op": "sum",
        "columns": ["quantity", "unit_price"],
        "group_by": "product",
        "key_column": "product",
        "value_column": "revenue"
    }
)

product_revenue_top5 = product_revenue_all.head(5).reset_index(drop=True)
emit_table("Top five products by revenue", product_revenue_top5)
emit_chart(
    "Top five products by revenue",
    "bar",
    product_revenue_top5,
    x="product",
    y="revenue",
    title="Top five products by revenue"
)

product_top5_share = (
    product_revenue_top5["revenue"].sum() / data["revenue"].sum()
    if data["revenue"].sum() != 0 else np.nan
)
emit_metric("Top five product revenue share", product_top5_share)

monthly_data = data.assign(
    month=data["parsed_order_date"].dt.to_period("M").astype(str)
)
monthly_revenue = (
    monthly_data.loc[monthly_data["parsed_order_date"].notna()]
    .groupby("month", as_index=False)["revenue"]
    .sum()
    .sort_values("month")
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
monthly_revenue["revenue_share"] = (
    monthly_revenue["revenue"] / data["revenue"].sum()
    if data["revenue"].sum() != 0 else np.nan
)
emit_table(
    "Monthly revenue",
    monthly_revenue,
    check={
        "op": "sum",
        "columns": ["quantity", "unit_price"],
        "group_by": "order_date",
        "key_column": "month",
        "value_column": "revenue",
        "time_grain": "month"
    }
)
emit_chart(
    "Monthly revenue comparison",
    "line",
    monthly_revenue,
    x="month",
    y="revenue",
    title="Monthly revenue comparison"
)

for column in ["order_date", "product", "quantity", "unit_price", "region"]:
    emit_metric(
        "Missing values in " + column,
        df[column].isna().sum(),
        check={"op": "count_missing", "columns": [column]}
    )

emit_metric(
    "Total missing cells",
    df.isna().sum().sum(),
    check={"op": "count_missing"}
)
emit_metric(
    "Duplicate rows",
    df.duplicated().sum(),
    check={"op": "count_duplicates"}
)

observations: The top five products were Laptop ($201,196.20), Monitor ($101,392.80), Standing Desk ($96,482.10), Headset ($63,599.55), and Office Chair ($58,336.10). Together, they represented 77.3% of revenue.
August had the highest monthly revenue at $77,556.75, followed by November at $73,143.20. February had the lowest revenue at $34,842.00.
There were no missing order dates. Missing values occurred in product (4), quantity (11), unit price (7), and region (8), for 30 missing cells overall.

The top-five product table is ranked by revenue.
Missing-value counts refer to individual cells, and duplicate rows are reported by the data-quality check.
